data.description:
## Story

As a developer, per-epic review cycles are recorded in a schema-versioned `cycle-ledger.json` file (stored in ARTIFACTS_DIR) using the existing cross-platform locking primitive, so the arbiter has a reliable, durable count of review cycles even across CI runners.

## Done Definitions

- [ ] `cycle-ledger.json` is written to `ARTIFACTS_DIR` (resolved from `deps.sh get_artifacts_dir`) using the cross-platform lock from S0; concurrent writes do not corrupt the file
- [ ] Schema includes at minimum: `schema_version` (string, semver), `epic_id`, `cycles` (array of objects with `cycle_num`, `timestamp_utc`, `findings_hash`)
- [ ] `contracts/cycle-ledger.md` exists and documents the schema, required fields, and allowed evolution rules (additive-only for minor versions)
- [ ] CI reconstruction path: when `cycle-ledger.json` is absent (ephemeral runner), the ledger is reconstructed from PR comments or ticket comments with `reconstruction_gaps: true` flag set in the output object; gaps do not block arbiter execution
- [ ] When `reconstruction_gaps: true`, arbiter logs a warning and treats missing cycles as unknown (does not assume cycle 0)
- [ ] Unit tests cover: normal write, concurrent-write lock contention (mocked), CI reconstruction from comments, reconstruction with partial data (reconstruction_gaps=true)
- [ ] Old cycle-count mechanism (if any inline counter exists in sprint or review workflow) is removed and replaced by ledger reads

## Considerations

- [Ordering] Must run after S0 (cross-platform lock) and S1 (max_cycles config rename); the ledger's cycle-cap logic reads `review.max_cycles`
- [Portability] ARTIFACTS_DIR path must be resolved at runtime via `get_artifacts_dir()` from `hooks/lib/deps.sh`; never hardcode `/tmp` paths
- [CI gap] PR comment reconstruction should parse `DSO-Review-Cycle:` trailer or equivalent structured marker — define the marker format in contracts/cycle-ledger.md before implementing reconstruction
- [Schema evolution] Use `schema_version: "1.0.0"` for initial release; document that readers must ignore unknown fields (forward-compat)
- [Escalation policy] Escalate when blocked
data.title: As a developer, per-epic review cycles are recorded in a schema-versioned cycle-ledger.json so the arbiter has durable cycle history
